result.title: Large language models underrepresent malice and overreport virtue
result.comment: 41 pages, 5 figures, 5 Extended Data figures, 2 Extended Data tables; Supplementary Information included
result.summary: People increasingly use large language models (LLMs) to interpret others' behaviour, often assuming that LLMs infer motives as humans do. Aligned LLMs attribute more benevolent and less malevolent motives to a whistleblower than humans do, but ratings alone cannot reveal whether these differences arise in internal representations or at report. Here we compare linear-probe readouts of LLMs' internal states with their own ratings at the same prompt position for four motives, in two preregistered studies. For the two malevolent motives, self-interest and intent to harm, internal and expressed readouts did not differ: the lower ratings reflect weaker signal along the probed directions, not suppression at output. For the two benevolent motives, duty and concern for others, expressed ratings exceeded the internal readouts, indicating amplification at report. In free text the model rarely volunteered a motive against the colleague, far less often than humans did, yet produced one readily once the scenario supplied a reason. Shifting the internal representation along a malevolent-motive direction brought both malevolent ratings to the human level, whereas the rating of duty yielded only past a threshold at which the other motives had overshot. LLMs' more charitable motive profile thus has two distinct sources: reduced malevolent signal in the probed representation and amplified benevolent attribution at report.

AI.brief_summary: 该文用两项预注册研究比较 LLM 对告密者动机的内部线性探针读数与同一位置的自陈评分，发现恶意动机（自利、伤害意图）差异源自表征信号更弱，而善意动机（责任、关心他人）在报告环节被放大，并可沿动机方向操控表征以改变评分。
AI.relevance_reason: 「同一提示位置探针读数 vs 输出评分 + 方向操控」的对照范式，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 内容究竟被答案使用、抑或仅在解码处被放大或抑制，以及内部信号强度与表述解离的测法。
